entry: METHOD: no rule for excerpts of real texts; bulverism LA1 (explaining a view after independent refutation)
fix: METHOD (b): add "If the passage is an excerpt of a longer real text and a condition fails only because support may be cut off at the excerpt boundary, record at most possible issue, and say what the full text would need to show." Add a "rhetorical notes (not fallacies)" field for charged or sectarian wording (here "jesuitically", "papistical"). Key: remove the error, or downgrade it to possible issue with a rhetorical note.
rationale: The motive clause comes after two independent replies: the turnabout ("the more shame upon her conduct") and the denial ("it happens not to be true"). The denial is argued in the very next sentence of Common Sense ("Europe, and not England, is the parent country of America"), so the bulverism look-alike applies in the full text. The anti-Catholic wording is loaded rhetoric, but no inference rests on it. F is right. E was forced to flag by the excerpt boundary and said so.

fault_class: answer key (overruled); method gap for rhetoric
entry: ad-hominem C3 / LA "insult not offered as a reason"; loaded-language LA2 (openly evaluative)
fix: Key: re-grade as legit, with a rhetorical note. The insult and the unsupported corruption claim describe who voted, and no conclusion is drawn from them; the argument rests on the study figures. METHOD: add a "rhetorical notes (not fallacies)" field so invective and unsupported accusations are recorded without a fallacy label.
rationale: Textbook ad hominem requires the attack to be offered as a reason to reject an argument. Here it isn't. Contrast R072 S4, where "But this is just another power grab" is offered in place of the merits the speaker has just conceded deserve debate. That one is correctly flagged.

entry: false-dilemma C1 ("presented as though ... the only ones"); METHOD (c) derivative steps
fix: false-dilemma C1: add "or the conclusion relies on an unstated two-way split, signalled by 'must' after one option is eliminated". METHOD (c): "a step that builds on an earlier error gets its own row if it commits a separate move of its own". With this, S4 -> flag (other origins: a person not named Mill, a later mill, a place name).
rationale: Both reviewers saw the move but C1 reads as needing explicit options.

entry: appeal-to-motive C1 "someone has made an argument"
fix: appeal-to-motive C1 and ad-hominem C1: "an argument, claim or proposal (a rule or policy counts)", matching circumstantial-ad-hominem.
rationale: E applied C1 literally. F read the proposal as an argument. The literal gap is the catalog's.

entry: no cross-family tie-break between generalization (converse accident) and comparison (false analogy)
fix: Add a cross-family rule, and a false-analogy look-alike: "if the source case is an exception (special population, special circumstances) and the conclusion is a rule for ordinary cases or everyone, use converse accident; false analogy is for carrying a conclusion from one case to another comparable case". converse-accident C1/C2 fit R031 exactly.
rationale: Both found the error. False analogy is a defensible description, but the catalog has a more specific entry that fits exactly, and nothing points reviewers to it.

entry: inflation-of-conflict has no family and no aliases; disregarding-known-science has no pointer to it
fix: Give inflation-of-conflict aliases ("appeal to controversy", "argument from expert disagreement", "manufactured doubt") and put it in a family (authority and popularity, or omitted evidence). Add to disregarding-known-science: "if the move is 'experts disagree on X, so nothing is known about Y', use inflation of conflict".
rationale: E's notes list "argument from expert disagreement" as a missing entry, but the catalog has it. It can't be reached through any family or alias.

F: possible issue equivocation; possible issue composition
fault_class: answer key (accept possible issue) + catalog (contested readings)
entry: METHOD: no rule for scholarly-disputed historical arguments
fix: METHOD: "For a well-known argument whose fallacy charge is disputed in the scholarly literature, name the classic charge, mark the row 'contested reading', and give possible issue unless the passage's own words settle it; state the reading under which it is a fallacy." Key: accept possible issue as correct as well as flag (its own note concedes the defence).
row_type: E/F verdict disagreement; F soft vs key
rationale: Both reviewers named the textbook charges (Moore). E flagged on the literal conditions; F used charity. Both are defensible for a disputed text.

entry: amphiboly C3 "context supports the other reading"
fix: amphiboly C3: "...the context, including the evident purpose of the document or rule, supports the other reading". Add look-alike: "both readings fit equally and nothing favours either -> possible issue". With this, R062 -> flag (a clause about what tenants may keep "in the unit" plainly concerns keeping; "under the lease as written" signals reliance on the convenient parse).
rationale: F required explicit drafter intent. The purpose of a lease clause is enough context.

E: possible issue equivocation (bulverism checked: no issue)
fault_class: answer key (overruled to contested) + catalog (excerpt rule)
entry: excerpt rule; bulverism LA1; tu-quoque C2
fix: Key: re-grade to contested, with possible issue correct. S3 gives a direct rebuttal (the real aim is to end women's status as instruments of production), so bulverism's look-alike applies. The "already exists" point is argued after the excerpt ends (bourgeois marriage, prostitution), so tu quoque vs equivocation can't be settled from the excerpt. Catalog: the excerpt rule (see R021).
row_type: key overconfident; E/F label split on possible issue
rationale: Both reviewers gave possible issue with different candidate entries, and both named what would settle it.

entry: appeal-to-nature C1 equivalents; no appeal-to-inevitability entry
fix: Add an entry, appeal to inevitability (fait accompli). C1: something is described as unavoidable or already here. C2: it is concluded to be good, beneficial or to be welcomed. C3: the inevitability is the step's reason. Look-alike: accepting and adapting to it, without approving. Add "survival of the fittest" and "law of nature" to the appeal-to-nature C1 equivalents. With these, the "It is here; we cannot evade it ... We accept and welcome, therefore ... as beneficial" step flags from the text, without relying on how "fittest" is read.
row_type: E/F verdict disagreement; F soft vs key
rationale: F's economic-efficiency reading is charitable but weak. The key's fallacy stands; possible issue is defensible.

entry: METHOD (g) "reports, quotes ... or satirises" vs multi-speaker items scored by speaker
fix: METHOD (g): "In a dialogue or exchange, score each participant's argument; a participant who advances an argument in direct speech is scored even if the author is satirising it (note the satire). Use no argument only when the passage's own voice narrates, teaches or mocks without a participant advancing it (R019 narrated anecdote, R042 authorial irony, R093 exercise)." Add a field, reported_fallacy, for no-issue rows that display a fallacy, so the information isn't lost.
rationale: E applied (g) literally and logged the conflict. F scored at speaker level, which is consistent with R030, R053, R060 and R090.

fix: Key: add S1 as a second error (unrepresentative sample / bad extrapolation; the method multiplies a count by an area, not a density). Possible issue is right; with "one corner" chosen and no density reasoning, a flag is arguable.
rationale: Both reviewers independently raised it, and F also logged the garbled method as an other error.

entry: METHOD (c) two errors
fix: Key: add ad hoc rescue as an acceptable second label for S3.
rationale: Explaining away contrary evidence is a separate move from projecting one's own experience.

entry: special-pleading C3
fix: C3: add "a bare self-assessment that one meets the purpose the rule exists to verify ('I know I can be impartial') does not count".

entry: accent written only for re-stressing
fix: C1: add "or real emphasis is read as implying a contrast the speaker plainly did not intend". Look-alike: the contrast is what the speaker meant.

entry: appeal-to-wealth C2 "in a respect unrelated to money"
fix: C2: "...unrelated to how the person became rich" (a claim about public spending is "about money" literally).

entry: causation family rule routes "the reason cases were selected into a group" to common cause
fix: Causation rule: "cases selected for an extreme value that then moved toward average -> regression fallacy, before common cause". Regression has to be checked before the common-cause step.
rationale: Both went against the literal rule.

entry: METHOD (c) second weak link in a chain; appeal-to-accomplishment LA "same field"
fix: METHOD (c): "a second weak link gets its own row if it meets an entry's conditions; otherwise note it as 'weak premise' without a label". appeal-to-accomplishment LA1: "same field and same skill (performing is not teaching)" (R026). modal-scope-fallacy: add the alias "idle argument / fatalism" for "nothing we do could change it, so don't act" (R029).
rationale: Not scored (the key doesn't count these).

entry: rule (g) correct identification vs straw-man C2
fix: METHOD (g): "the rebuttal's logic is judged under (g); whether the rebutted view is fairly attributed is a straw-man check, made only when a specific opponent and their words are identifiable in the passage".
